items.title: Indivisible Greater West Loop plans its 2027 agenda and a Dec. 9 book club meeting
items.summary: Indivisible Greater West Loop says it is drafting its 2027 strategy across national, city and neighborhood priorities and will send members a survey soon. Its in-person book club meets Dec. 9 to discuss "Jesus and John Wayne," and Indivisible National hosts a virtual launch of its new guide and strategic plan on Thursday, Dec. 10. The group also reported raising more than $525 for the Chicagoland Food Sovereignty Coalition and collecting a carload of toys for the Pilsen Food Pantry.

items.title: Local Indivisible group urges calls on Senate leadership vote and a data center permitting bill
items.summary: This week's Indivisible Greater West Loop action plan asks members to contact Sen. Tammy Duckworth and Senator-elect Juliana Stratton about the Senate Democratic leadership vote expected by Dec. 1, in which Sen. Chris Van Hollen is challenging Chuck Schumer. It also asks residents to call their U.S. representative to oppose the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, an energy permitting bill that has passed the Senate and would fast-track data center development.

items.title: Seven lawmakers in the running for Illinois House speaker
items.summary: Seven state representatives have told the House Democratic caucus they intend to run for speaker: Eva-Dina Delgado, Will Davis, Ann Williams, Kam Buckner, Marcus Evans, Jay Hoffman and Jehan Gordon-Booth. Delgado is the only one who signed a letter calling on Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch to step down over his handling of a sexual harassment claim, and lawmakers are split on whether that should be a litmus test. Candidates are expected to pitch colleagues Dec. 1 through 3, with a caucus vote during the January lame-duck session before the Jan. 13 swearing-in.

items.title: Poll puts Mayor Johnson's approval at 31% ahead of the February election
items.summary: A One Future Illinois survey of likely Chicago voters, taken Nov. 15 to 18, found 31% approve of Mayor Brandon Johnson's job performance and 69% disapprove, close to the 33% and 34% approval it measured in September and June. Just 19% said he has done a good job on the city's budget and finances. POLITICO notes the poll was conducted by a group supporting aldermen who oppose the mayor's budget proposal.

items.title: South and West Side drivers get booted at twice the citywide rate
items.summary: A WBEZ analysis highlighted in POLITICO Illinois Playbook found drivers on Chicago's South and West sides have their vehicles booted at two times the citywide rate. Separately, some City Council members say a contract extension for the Chicago Park District CEO is premature before next year's mayoral election.

items.title: United expects nearly 640,000 O'Hare departures over Thanksgiving
items.summary: United Airlines says Chicago Thanksgiving bookings are up 5% from last year and expects nearly 640,000 passengers to depart O'Hare between Nov. 19 and Dec. 1, with Sunday, Nov. 29 the busiest day. The airline is adding biometric bag drops, automated boarding gates and a River North location where travelers can check luggage the night before. INRIX expects the worst road traffic Tuesday and Wednesday before the holiday and Sunday and Monday after it.

items.title: Work begins on O'Hare's $917 million Concourse E
items.summary: The city broke ground last week on O'Hare's new Concourse E, a $917 million project that will add 24 gates to the airport. The concourse is expected to be completed in 2034, and the city has released renderings of the design.

items.title: Britain weighs how far to go in reversing Brexit after EU summit
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast reports British Prime Minister Andy Burnham signed deals at a Nov. 20 EU-U.K. summit in Brussels easing food and drink trade barriers, creating a youth visa swap and linking carbon trading. Burnham has said "all options" should be on the table, including rejoining the EU, but Cabinet members are divided and he now calls the effort an informal brainstorming process. U.N. climate talks at COP31 in Turkey also collapsed this weekend without an agreement.

items.title: LiveLaunch brings online brands to a West Loop showroom for one day, Nov. 28
items.summary: On Saturday, Nov. 28, LiveLaunch at 810 W. Washington Blvd. opens its floor to brands that normally sell only online. Nothing is sold on site; visitors scan a code to buy, book or join with a brand online, with orders shipping in time for the holidays. An industry night for creators, designers and partners runs Friday, Nov. 27 from 5 p.m.

items.title: Christmas tree lighting celebrations set for Chicago's Greektown, Lakeview communities
items.summary: The holiday season was getting into gear in Chicago on Sunday, with tree-lighting ceremonies planned in Greektown and Lakeview.

items.title: Holiday kickoff ceremonies set for Greektown, Lakeview
items.summary: The holiday season was getting into gear in Chicago on Sunday, with tree-lighting ceremonies planned in Greektown and Lakeview.

items.title: Suzanne and Shane visit the Walnut Room, leaves on trees at golden hour | What Caught My Eye
items.summary: Recently, meteorologist Shane Hinton asked Suzanne Le Mignot about Chicago's holiday traditions and invited her to the Walnut Room at Macy’s. Meanwhile, Shane himself took notice of the autumn leaves on the trees at golden hour in Skinner Park in the West Loop.

items.title: Video shows rollover crash in Chicago's River North neighborhood
items.summary: Video shows a rollover crash in downtown Chicago Sunday.

items.title: Chicago police investigating string of business burglaries in South Loop
items.summary: Thieves stolen cash registers from at least four business after breaking in through the front glass early Saturday in the city's South Loop neighborhood, Chicago police said.

items.title: Thousands turn out for Magnificent Mile Lights Festival, parade downtown
items.summary: Chicago was illuminated with even more holiday cheer thanks to the 35th year of the Magnificent Mile Lights Festival on Saturday.

items.title: Cash registers stolen during burglaries reported minutes apart in South Loop
items.summary: Cash registers were stolen during burglaries in Chicago's South Loop early Saturday morning.

items.title: Small Business Saturday: Heritage Press & Blow Dry
items.summary: Stop by Heritage Press & Blow Dry in Chicago's West Loop.

items.title: Man, woman shot and killed outside hookah lounge in West Town
items.summary: Two people were killed in a shooting outside a hookah lounge in Chicago's West Town neighborhood.

items.title: 2 killed in shooting outside hookah lounge in West Town
items.summary: Two people were killed in a shooting outside a hookah lounge in Chicago's West Town neighborhood.

items.title: Magnificent Mile Lights Festival returns to Michigan Avenue in downtown Chicago on Saturday
items.summary: As the holiday season gets underway, the 35th annual Magnificent Mile Lights Festival kicks off on Saturday morning in downtown Chicago.

items.title: Magnificent Mile Lights Festival set for Saturday
items.summary: As the holiday season gets underway, the 35th annual Magnificent Mile Lights Festival kicks off on Saturday morning in downtown Chicago.

items.title: S&P puts Chicago's credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade
items.summary: S&P Global Ratings has placed Chicago under review for a possible credit downgrade, putting fresh attention on City Hall's fiscal management as it works to close an $882 million budget gap. Civic Federation President Joe Ferguson warned that "dysfunction matters," pointing to strained relations between the mayor and the City Council. A rating decision could come within 90 days, about a week before the Feb. 23 mayoral election.

items.title: State Rep. Ann Williams joins the race for Illinois House Speaker
items.summary: Chicago Democrat Ann Williams, who has served in the Illinois House since 2011, is running to replace House Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch. She is pitching herself as a consensus builder who can work across the caucus. The leadership contest has gained momentum after 26 House Democrats called for new leadership.

items.title: Illinois Senate names "Loop the Cart" the official state recycling mascot
items.summary: The Illinois Senate on Wednesday approved a resolution sponsored by Sen. Julie Morrison naming "Loop the Cart" the state's official recycling mascot. The resolution also recognizes the Chicago Metro Recycling Education and Outreach collaboration and its "Feed The Cart" campaign. The House is expected to take up a companion measure after Thanksgiving, which would make Illinois the first state with a legislatively designated recycling mascot.

items.title: Cook County Board passes $9.76 billion budget
items.summary: The Cook County Board of Commissioners easily passed the county's $9.76 billion budget, according to the Chicago Tribune. The vote wraps up the county's budget process for the coming year while the City of Chicago's own budget fight continues.

items.title: Europe's leaders project unity on Ukraine after the Shenzhen summit
items.summary: Dozens of members of the Europe-led "Coalition of the Willing" met in Berlin to show unified support for Ukraine after the U.S., China and Russia held a three-way summit in Shenzhen. European Council President Antonio Costa said Europe has "a strong negotiating team, a unified voice and a clear goal." POLITICO reports concern that France's presidential runoff next May could weaken that support.

items.title: Federal judge lets Illinois keep enforcing its hemp THC restrictions
items.summary: U.S. District Judge Martha Pacold declined Thursday to temporarily block Illinois' new hemp law, which took effect Nov. 12 and treats products with more than 0.4 milligrams of total THC per container as cannabis sold only in licensed dispensaries. Some THC beverage makers have already stopped selling in Illinois or moved operations out of state. The hemp businesses are considering an appeal.

items.title: Regulators approve about a third of Peoples Gas' requested rate increase
items.summary: The Illinois Commerce Commission approved $40.3 million of Peoples Gas' rate increase request, less than a third of what the utility originally sought. Peoples Gas is the natural gas utility for Chicago homes and businesses. Details are in WTTW's coverage.

items.title: Free coat and turkey giveaway Saturday at Teamster City
items.summary: The 34th Ward office is holding a coat and turkey giveaway on Saturday, Nov. 21 at 9:30 a.m. at Teamster City, 1645 W. Jackson Blvd. Coats and turkeys are available while supplies last. Volunteers are still needed to help run the event.

items.title: Thanksgiving week: recycling changes and parade street closures
items.summary: City offices and the 34th Ward office close Nov. 26-27. Streets and Sanitation (Zones 2 and 4) will skip recycling pickup on Thursday, Nov. 26, while LRS zones move Friday pickup to Saturday. The Chicago Thanksgiving Parade steps off at Ida B. Wells Dr. and State St. at 7:45 a.m. on Nov. 26, with rolling closures from 4 a.m. to 2 p.m., and State Street between Washington and Randolph closes at 10 a.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

items.title: Soul City Church expansion to include noise mitigation for neighbors
items.summary: After neighbors raised concerns about noise from Soul City Church's existing auditorium at a community meeting on its proposed expansion, the design team proposed a suspended acoustic ceiling below the auditorium roof to reduce noise heard outside. The noise plan must be included in the church's application before city planning bodies consider the expansion.

items.title: WCA holiday party Dec. 8 doubles as a toiletries drive for the 12th District
items.summary: The West Central Association holds its holiday party Tuesday, Dec. 8 from 5 to 8 p.m. at Blind Barber, a ticketed event for members and guests. Guests are invited to bring new, unopened toiletries for the Chicago Police 12th District's hygiene drive for unhoused people and veterans, including soap, toothpaste, toothbrushes, deodorant, wipes and socks.

items.title: 26 Things To Do In Chicago This Weekend: Tree Lightings, Mag Mile Lights Festival And More
items.summary: The opening of Zoo Lights, a printmaking festival, holiday markets, tailgate parties and more are also on deck.

items.title: This 12-Year-Old Violinist Will Make Symphony Center Debut As Youth Orchestra’s Youngest Member
items.summary: Tentana Kahar will perform Sunday in the fall concert of the elite ensemble’s premier group.

items.title: Sky Ride Tap, a 93-year-old Loop dive bar, closes at year's end
items.summary: Sky Ride Tap, the Loop dive bar known for its throwback signage on Van Buren near Dearborn, will close at the end of 2026 after 93 years. It joins a list of longtime Chicago-area businesses shutting down this year, including the 66-year-old American Sale chain, which is liquidating its seven suburban stores but plans to stay open into early 2027.

items.title: City Council orders review of CFO's abrupt resignation
items.summary: The City Council voted 45 in favor of reviewing the Nov. 13 resignation of chief financial officer Ashlee Gabrysch, who said staying in the role would compromise her integrity after disputing how much of the deficit was being closed with structural revenue (the administration said 76%, she calculated 56%). The administration countered with calls to investigate her handling of a $75 million pension payment. S&P put the city's credit rating on notice the same day.

items.title: Rashid Johnson retrospective opens at the MCA
items.summary: "Rashid Johnson: A Poem for Deep Thinkers," a mid-career retrospective of the Chicago-raised artist, is now open at the Museum of Contemporary Art. Highlights include "Antoine's Oregon," a massive plant-covered structure that hides a working organ, and the debut of the video "Home: A Poem." The show runs through April 25, 2027.

items.title: City Council backs a statewide millionaires tax and revives gunshot-detection contract
items.summary: At a special meeting Wednesday, the Chicago City Council voted unanimously to support a statewide millionaires tax. Members also voted to require the city to move forward with a contract for gunshot-detection technology and approved an independent investigation into how the city's finances were presented. S&P Global Ratings has warned Chicago it is at risk of another credit downgrade.

items.title: State proposes keeping 11 oil and gas plants open longer as data center demand grows
items.summary: The Illinois Power Agency and EPA proposed delaying the retirement of 11 oil and gas power plants by up to three years past their 2030 and 2031 shutdown dates under the 2021 Clean and Equitable Jobs Act, citing grid reliability and utility bills. Coal plant closure dates are unchanged. A September state analysis estimated Illinois' power supply must more than double by 2045, largely because of hyperscale data centers. The Illinois Commerce Commission must approve the change next year.

items.title: Business leader backs millionaires tax while criticizing City Hall's tone
items.summary: Accepting the Chicagoland Chamber of Commerce's Burnham Award before 700-plus guests at the Hyatt Regency, GCM Grosvenor CEO Michael Sacks said he supports a millionaires tax, tied to the base income tax rate, with revenue shared with Chicago and a lockbox on how it is spent. He also sharply criticized the mayor's leadership style, comparing it to President Trump's.

items.title: State Rep. Eva-Dina Delgado enters race for Illinois House Speaker
items.summary: State Rep. Eva-Dina Delgado, an assistant majority leader representing Chicago's 3rd District, announced she is running to succeed House Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch. She is pitching her experience as a co-budgeteer who helped broker the state's transit overhaul and clean energy legislation. Before joining the House in 2019, she held government affairs roles at the CTA and Peoples Gas.

items.title: Forum Cafe opens on a historic Bronzeville block
items.summary: Forum Cafe opened this week at 318 E. 43rd St., next to Metropolis Art Gallery and the historic Forum Hall, which opened in 1897 and closed in the 1970s. Owner Bernard Loyd bought the 318-322 E. 43rd St. complex in 2011 for $100,000 and sees it as the anchor for reviving the stretch by the 43rd Street Green Line stop. Reginald Robinson performs and talks about the Forum's ragtime history there Friday at 5:30 p.m.

items.title: Public defender proposes immediate lawyer access for every arrestee
items.summary: The Cook County Public Defender's Office proposes giving every arrestee immediate access to a phone and its 24/7 hotline when read their rights, aiming to prevent false confessions like those behind a recent $260 million settlement. The office says 91% of people questioned by CPD for the most serious crimes in 2023 and 2024 did not consult a lawyer. The mayor's office called the idea a meaningful safeguard; CPD and the FOP did not comment.

items.title: City makes its case in Springfield for a Chicago Bears stadium
items.summary: A top mayoral adviser lobbied legislators at the Capitol on Bears stadium proposals, CPS funding and data centers, saying four developer concepts show Chicago can host a new stadium. Lawmakers are weighing a municipal stadium authority that would own a new domed stadium, with the Bears paying to build it and public financing covering roads and other surrounding infrastructure.

items.title: Appeals court fast-tracks challenge to three mayoral candidates' eligibility
items.summary: Mayoral candidate Bill Quinlan is appealing the dismissal of his lawsuit arguing that Illinois law bars Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias, Rep. Mike Quigley and County Treasurer Maria Pappas from running for mayor while holding other offices. A Cook County judge ruled last month the issue should go first to the election board; the appellate court on Tuesday put the case on an accelerated track.

items.title: Bill would let Illinoisans opt out of political text messages
items.summary: State Rep. Bob Morgan introduced legislation creating a free, statewide opt-out registry for political texts. Political texting companies would be barred from knowingly using or selling numbers on the list for mass political messaging.

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin meet for first three-way summit in Shenzhen
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast reports President Trump arrived in Shenzhen ahead of the first-ever trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, where he hopes to reach a nuclear non-proliferation agreement. The Kremlin said no more than an hour has been set aside for the meeting. European leaders worry about concessions to Russia on Ukraine.

items.title: Europe sends seven negotiators to Ukraine peace talks
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast reports European leaders agreed that national security advisers from Germany, Britain, France, Italy and Poland, plus two senior EU officials, will all take part in revived Russia-Ukraine peace talks rather than a single lead negotiator. POLITICO's Nick Vinocur called it a compromise that exposes the EU's lack of a coherent foreign policy.

items.title: The Nov. 18 Skyline is out
items.summary: The new edition of Skyline is out. Editor Tom O'Gorman's note to readers is brief: he hopes you will enjoy the issue. The full issue is available from Inside Publications.

items.title: Ald. Pat Dowell Facing 2 Challengers In 3rd Ward Race
items.summary: South Loop resident Raheem Uqdah, a Democratic Socialist, and Bronzeville native Qushona Harris are also contenders for the 3rd Ward seat.

items.title: Bally’s Says $560 Million In New Loans Will Help Secure Spring Opening For Chicago Casino
items.summary: The funding comes as Bally's pushes forward on the $1.8 billion project amid mounting debt, construction setbacks and millions in losses.

items.title: Love Language' Is The Rare 21st-Century Rom-Com Filmed Entirely In Chicago
items.summary: The romantic comedy starring Chloë Grace Moretz, Anthony Ramos, Manny Jacinto and Billie Lourd was recently released in select theaters and on streaming services.

items.title: Cubs’ Wrigley Field Parking Expansion Advances, Along With Briar St. Theatre Conversion, Other Projects
items.summary: Ald. Bennett Lawson (44th) backed a revised plan for more parking spaces near Wrigley Field. Other proposals would bring apartments to Logan Square, Lakeview and West Loop.

items.title: Blue Man Group Returns To Chicago For Special Holiday Show
items.summary: "A New Holiday Surprise" opens Nov. 24 and runs through Dec. 13 at Broadway in Chicago's CIBC Theatre Downtown.

items.title: 2nd Ward Ald. Brian Hopkins Faces First Challenger In Reelection Bid
items.summary: Both candidates are also facing challenges to their petitions which will test the validity of their campaigns.

items.title: CTA Cuts 13 Bus Stops On Damen In Effort To Quicken Your Commute
items.summary: The changes impact stops along a stretch of Damen Avenue between West Town and the Lower West Side.

items.title: CTA Safe Ride Specialists Are Only A Start' To Improving Safety On Transit, Riders Say
items.summary: The yearlong pilot launched in October, deploying non-law enforcement workers trained in crisis intervention to help riders in need and connect people with resources.

items.title: Illinois lawmakers weigh first statewide data center rules
items.summary: The POWER Act, expected to move during the veto session that starts today, would require large data centers to bring their own renewable energy, disclose their water and electricity use, and stop signing nondisclosure agreements with local governments. Versions of the bill have circulated in Springfield for more than a year, opposed by building trade unions. Voters nationally passed 40 of 41 local ballot measures regulating data centers in this month's election, according to Ballotpedia.

items.title: Public comment open on $5 billion regional transit budget through Dec. 4
items.summary: NITA, the new agency overseeing the CTA, Metra and Pace, has released a $5 billion 2027 budget proposal and is taking public comment through Dec. 4. CTA riders logged more than 100 train delays of 10 minutes or more in October. Last month the CTA launched Safe Ride Specialists, trained to connect riders experiencing homelessness, mental health crises or substance use with housing, treatment and services.

items.title: Veto session opens with leadership races and Bears stadium talks
items.summary: Lawmakers return to Springfield today as House Democrats jockey to succeed Speaker Chris Welch, who is not seeking another term; named contenders include state Reps. Kam Buckner, Eva-Dina Delgado, Jehan Gordon-Booth, Jay Hoffman, Ann Williams and Marcus Evans. Republicans in both chambers face leadership challenges after midterm losses. A plan that could give both Chicago and Arlington Heights a shot at a Bears stadium is still being negotiated, with a December vote considered more likely than one this week. Data center rules and Chicago school funding are also unfinished.

items.title: How Chicago reached $55 billion in debt
items.summary: A WTTW and ProPublica project traces Chicago's $55 billion debt to three main causes: state legislation that let the city contribute less to pensions each year than was needed, the long-term parking meter lease, and hundreds of millions of dollars in police misconduct settlements. Separately, aldermen introduced an ordinance allowing an outside investigation of city finances following the city CFO's departure, with a vote planned this week.

items.title: Mayoral candidate releases audit of city staffing since 2019
items.summary: Chicago mayoral candidate George Cardenas released an analysis of budgeted city positions finding that since 2019 budgets cut 1,232 police officer positions while adding 377 management and appointed jobs. His campaign says management payroll rose 39%, from $291 million to $405 million. Cardenas proposes freezing non-union hiring, auditing management positions added since 2019 and redirecting savings to front-line workers such as police officers and 911 call-takers.

items.title: Nvidia faces first earnings call since CEO resignation
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast reports Big Tech stocks fell ahead of Nvidia's Q3 earnings call, the first since co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. Interim CEO Colette Kress, the longtime chief financial officer, is expected to face questions about the company's direction and its role financing AI infrastructure. Nvidia's board has signaled it intends to move on without Huang.

items.title: Shop Local 2026: A Bronzeville And South Loop Gift Guide
items.summary: From candles and fragrances to dance classes and stylish clothing, you can’t go wrong with this year’s Bronzeville and South Loop gift guide.

items.title: Shop Local 2026: A Downtown, West Loop And Gold Coast Gift Guide
items.summary: From local fine art, jewlery, skincare and cool sports merch, West Loop and Downtown offer an abundance of holiday shopping options.

items.title: Shop Local 2026: Your Guide To Chicago’s Holiday Markets
items.summary: Take advantage of a wide variety of markets in neighborhoods across the city for your holiday shopping this year.

items.title: Shop Local 2026: An Immigrant-Owned Businesses Gift Guide
items.summary: Shop for herbal tea, flowers, bonbons, jewelry, Mexican crafts, Turkish lamps and more at these six immigrant-owned businesses in Chicago.

items.title: Sky Ride Tap Closing After 93 Years In The Loop
items.summary: Kyriakos "Carl" Damianides, who has run the bar since 1972, said the building was recently sold and the new owner wants all remaining businesses out. Its last night will be New Year's Eve.

items.title: Paint-and-sip fundraiser Nov. 18 and holiday toy drive Nov. 21 for local food groups
items.summary: Indivisible Greater West Loop is hosting a paint-and-sip holiday fundraiser with Chicago Sip & Paint on Wednesday, Nov. 18, from 6 to 8:30 p.m., with part of each ticket going to the Chicago Food Sovereignty Coalition. On Saturday, Nov. 21, from 8 to 11:30 a.m., the group is collecting new, unwrapped toys valued over $15 for the Pilsen Food Pantry at the last farmers market of the year. Details and tickets are on the group's Mobilize calendar.

items.title: Springfield veto session: bills on data centers, pricing, guns, voting and foam foodware
items.summary: With the Illinois General Assembly back in Springfield for its veto session, Indivisible Greater West Loop is urging residents to contact state legislators about several bills. They include the POWER Act on data center energy and water use, a ban on surveillance pricing, the RIFL Act (SB 2279) on firearm manufacturer accountability, the RACE Act (HB 5414/SB 2983) on voting rights for incarcerated people, and a polystyrene foam foodware phase-out (SB 1531). Indivisible National's virtual launch of its new guide and strategic plan has moved to Thursday, Dec. 10.

items.title: Trump heads to Asia for a week of trade and defense summits
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast reports President Trump leaves for Asia for the ASEAN summit in Manila and the APEC summit in China, ending with a planned three-way meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Asian diplomats told POLITICO they expect less appetite for deals after Republican losses in this month's midterms. The White House says Trump aims to finalize a long-negotiated trade deal with Thailand.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson appoints Mike Belsky as acting city CFO amid budget controversy
items.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson named former Highland Park mayor Mike Belsky as Chicago's acting chief financial officer, replacing Ashlee Gabrysch who resigned after three months. Gabrysch had challenged the mayor's claim that 76% of the budget fix was structural, pointing to $480 million in borrowing for police misconduct settlements. The shake‑up has drawn criticism from state Comptroller Susana Mendoza and mayoral candidates, who accuse the administration of fiscal mismanagement.

items.title: Citadel CEO Ken Griffin vows to block Gov. JB Pritzker's White House ambitions
items.summary: Citadel founder and CEO Ken Griffin, who relocated to Florida, said in a Financial Times interview that he will work to keep Illinois Governor JB Pritzker from reaching the White House. Griffin criticized Pritzker's policies as politically motivated and accused him of sacrificing Illinois residents for personal ambition. The rivalry dates back to 2018 and includes Griffin's support for Republican candidates and opposition to Pritzker's graduated income tax proposal.

items.title: Waymo stalled in Chicago
items.summary: Humans still drive Waymo robotaxis in Chicago, and legislation to change that is stuck in the Illinois House. State lawmakers face a consequential choice over whether to allow robotaxis to operate in Illinois while still protecting rideshare drivers and unions who oppose the technology. The fall veto session kicks off tomorrow when the Illinois General Assembly may consider autonomous vehicle (AV) legislation.

items.title: Chicago aldermen push for ShotSpotter and millionaire tax after voter approval
items.summary: A coalition of Chicago aldermen in the City Council Budget Accountability Coalition announced plans to call for votes on two advisory measures that voters supported last week: reinstating the ShotSpotter gunshot detection policy, which the mayor ended in September 2024, and a millionaire’s tax that the mayor also backs. The coalition will seek votes at next week’s City Council meeting as Mayor Brandon Johnson’s proposed 2027 budget still lacks the 26 votes needed for passage before the Dec. 31 deadline.

items.title: Merchants sue over federal exemption of banks from Illinois swipe‑fee ban
items.summary: Retailers filed lawsuits claiming federal regulators overstepped authority by exempting national banks and credit unions from Illinois’ law that bars credit and debit card swipe fees on sales taxes and tips. The merchants argue the exemption undermines the state’s effort to eliminate swipe fees, and the lawsuits were reported by Bloomberg Law’s Evan Weinberger.

items.title: CTA seeks rider input in 34th Ward Bus Vision Project
items.summary: CTA invites residents to share feedback on bus service as part of its Bus Vision Project. A community engagement meeting will be held on November 17 from 5‑7 pm at CTA headquarters, 567 W. Lake. Riders can also take an online survey or learn more on the project website.

items.title: Greektown hosts annual Christmas tree lighting and cultural celebration
items.summary: The Greektown Annual Christmas Tree Celebration takes place on November 22 from 3:30 pm to 5 pm at Elysian Field on the southeast corner of Halsted & Van Buren. The event features Santa, a tree lit in the Greek flag colors, carols sung by local Greek school students, and complimentary hot chocolate and loukoumades. The National Hellenic Museum will also be open for free and host a Cider & Cookies gathering from 3‑5 pm.

items.title: South Loop Farmers Market reopens at Printers Row Park
items.summary: The South Loop Farmers Market returns to Printers Row Park, located at 632 S. Dearborn St, operating Saturdays from 9 am to 1 pm through November 21. The market showcases dozens of local farmers and food producers, providing residents an opportunity to support local businesses and connect with neighbors.

items.title: CTA Bus Vision Project Seeks Community Input on Future Bus Service
items.summary: CTA is gathering feedback through its Bus Vision Project to shape future bus service and investments. Residents can complete an online survey by November 30 and enter to win one of five $100 digital Visa gift cards. An open house is scheduled at CTA Headquarters (567 W. Lake St.) on November 17 from 5 to 7 p.m.

items.title: Retailers sue federal regulators over exemptions to Illinois swipe‑fee ban
items.summary: A pair of lawsuits filed by merchants allege that federal regulators overstepped authority by creating rules that exempt national banks and credit unions from Illinois’ law prohibiting credit‑card swipe fees on sales taxes and tips. The retailers claim the exemptions undermine the state’s effort to eliminate these fees and hurt local businesses. The lawsuits were reported by Bloomberg Law’s Evan Weinberger.

items.title: CTA Bus Vision Project holds community engagement meeting in the 34th Ward
items.summary: CTA is seeking input from riders and non‑riders as part of its Bus Vision Project, and a community engagement meeting is scheduled for November 17 from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. at the CTA headquarters located at 567 W. Lake. Residents of the 34th Ward are invited to share feedback on how bus service can better serve their neighborhoods. Additional information, including a survey and event details, is available on the project website.

items.title: O’Hare Flyer Express Connection Proposal Discussed at WCA Speaker Series
items.summary: The West Central Association hosted a speaker‑series luncheon on November 17 to discuss a proposed 15‑minute express connection from downtown Chicago to O’Hare, featuring the O’Hare Flyer team. The event included a Q&A, lunch catered by Canal Street Eatery, and networking at the Platform Conference Center, 320 S. Canal St. It also served as the WCA’s annual meeting.

items.title: 410 N. Elizabeth Construction Milestone Reached
items.summary: The construction project at 410 N. Elizabeth has reached a significant milestone, marking progress toward the development of the property in the West Loop. The newsletter notes the milestone but does not provide further details on the project's scope or timeline.

items.title: 2 injured, vehicle crashes into building in the Loop after driver runs red light, Chicago police say
items.summary: Two people were injured and a vehicle crashed into a building Saturday morning in the Loop after a driver ran a red light, Chicago police said.

items.title: Chicago City Council aldermen push for ShotSpotter reinstatement and millionaire tax after voter support
items.summary: The Chicago City Council Budget Accountability Coalition, a group of aldermen, announced plans to call votes on two voter‑backed measures at next week’s council meeting: restoring the ShotSpotter gunshot detection system and adopting a millionaire’s tax. Mayor Brandon Johnson supports the tax but previously ended the ShotSpotter contract in September 2024. The coalition argues that voters sent two clear messages and the mayor cannot select only the one he prefers. The push comes as the mayor’s proposed 2027 budget still lacks the 26 votes needed for passage before the Dec. 31 deadline.

items.title: Retailers sue federal regulators over Illinois swipe‑fee ban exemption
items.summary: A pair of lawsuits filed by merchants allege that federal regulators exceeded their authority by exempting national banks and credit unions from Illinois’ law prohibiting credit and debit card swipe fees on sales taxes and tips. The retailers claim the exemption undermines the state’s effort to eliminate swipe fees for consumers and businesses. The lawsuits seek to block the exemption and enforce the swipe‑fee ban statewide.

items.title: CTA Bus Vision Project seeks rider input with 34th Ward meeting
items.summary: CTA is gathering feedback on its Bus Vision Project; a community engagement meeting will be held on November 17 from 5‑7 pm at CTA headquarters, 567 W. Lake, inviting riders and non‑riders to share ideas on improving bus service across the region.

items.title: Illinois lawmakers push Bears stadium deal to keep team in state

Bill Cunningham is leading negotiations on a stadium-authority model that would let a municipality build a privately financed, publicly owned stadium, aiming to keep the Chicago Bears in Illinois. The proposal seeks to avoid taxpayer liability while offering incentives for mega projects, and faces scrutiny from both Democratic and Republican leaders.

Biggs was backed by the union representing Chicago Public School support staff and the Common Ground Collective super PAC. Her victory makes her the first elected president of the CPS board.

items.title: Democratic lawmakers organize opposition to Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch in Illinois House
items.summary: A group of Democratic state representatives is quietly trying to organize opposition to Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch ahead of a speaker vote expected in January. Lawmakers cite Welch's handling of a sexual harassment complaint involving former Rep. Harry Benton, a 60‑vote rule for measures, and broader frustrations with House operations. The effort reflects growing tension in Springfield as legislators prepare for the upcoming veto session.

items.title: Gov. JB Pritzker wins third term and unveils “Fighting for Illinois” agenda
items.summary: Incumbent Governor JB Pritzker defeated Republican Darren Bailey on Nov. 3, 2026 to win a third term. After his victory speech at Chicago’s Navy Pier, he introduced the “Fighting for Illinois: The Day One Agenda,” a set of nearly 200 policy proposals aimed at addressing everyday challenges. The agenda was presented as part of his plan to fight for Illinois at the state and federal levels.

items.title: City Hall hosts mobile food car licensing ordinance rally
items.summary: At 9 a.m. on Nov. 4, 2026, city officials gathered at City Hall for a rally on a new mobile food car licensing ordinance. The event, featuring remarks by Brandon, aimed to discuss the proposed licensing rules for mobile food vendors and coincided with an online Native American Heritage Month cultural reception.

items.title: The Nov. 4 Skyline is out
items.summary: The Nov. 4, 2026 edition of Skyline is out, a day after the midterm election. Editor Tom O'Gorman says more election results are still coming in and the paper will keep reporting on them. The full issue is available from Inside Publications.

items.title: Illinois' blue wave
items.summary: Illinois voters turned out yesterday in an election marked by long lines, sporadic polling-place problems and historic results. Yesterday's results will shape Illinois' political leadership and representation in Washington, while offering a glimpse of how Chicago voters may feel about Mayor Brandon Johnson and the Chicago Teachers Union. (more on that below) Gov.

items.title: State Rep. La Shawn Ford Wins Race To Succeed Danny Davis In 7th Congressional District
items.summary: Ford will be the district's first new leader in 30 years, replacing the retiring U.S. Rep. Danny Davis.

items.title: What to expect after the midterm results
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast laid out what to watch once Tuesday's midterm results came in, including a likely return to divided government in Washington if Democrats win the House. It expects more legislative gridlock, budget standoffs, and a wave of congressional investigations, along with the immediate start of the 2028 presidential contest in both parties.

items.title: Voting underway at Loop Supersite
items.summary: Darius Johnson reports live from the Loop Supersite. Lines are under 30 minutes, and Darius said voting takes around 10 minutes once inside.

items.title: Black Harvest Film Festival Celebrates 32nd Year With Lineup For Us, By Us'
items.summary: The festival showcasing films created by Black artists returns to the School of the Art Institute of Chicago’s Gene Siskel Film Center Friday through Nov. 15 with 10 shorts as well as feature-length films.

items.title: Chicago school board president race pits CTU‑backed Hilario Dominguez against SEIU‑endorsed Jessica Biggs
items.summary: The contest for Chicago school board president has CTU‑backed Hilario Dominguez framing the fight as a stand against outside influence, while billionaire Michael Sacks backs his opponent Jessica Biggs, who is supported by two SEIU groups. The race is seen as an early test of the city’s progressive coalition and could signal trends for the February mayoral election. Both CTU and SEIU are prominent progressive labor groups in Chicago.

items.title: Illinois Democrats raise record $141.85 million through ActBlue in 2026 midterms
items.summary: ActBlue reported that Illinois Democrats collected $141.85 million in the 2026 midterm cycle, a 15.5 percent increase over 2022, with 1.04 million donors contributing 6.7 percent more than four years ago. ActBlue CEO Regina Wallace‑Jones highlighted the surge during a Chicago stop on her cross‑country tour, handing out coffee and donuts to voters. The fundraising boost positions Illinois as a strong blue pillar in the Midwest.

items.title: Election storylines to watch
items.summary: Illinois voters head to the polls today to decide who will lead the state, represent them in Washington and oversee Chicago's public schools. Beyond the marquee races for governor and U. Senate, the results could reshape political power in our area for years to come.

items.title: Polls open for Illinois 2026 midterm election
items.summary: As Darious Johnson reports, voters are already lined up outside the Loop supersite.

items.title: Woman issues warning after Uber driver cancels ride, drives wrong way mid-trip
items.summary: Her Uber app shows a location on Hubbard as the drop-off address, but she says they were able to finally get out of the car on Randolph Street near the Kennedy Expressway.

items.title: Neon Trees, Michael James Scott, Thelma Houston To Headline Magnificent Mile Lights Parade
items.summary: The 35th annual festival and parade returns Saturday, Nov. 21 with live performances, floats, a fireworks spectacular and one million lights along Michigan Avenue.
